facts.value: Some of the library's manuscripts are written on deer-skin and cloth as well as paper and palm leaf.
facts.quote: written on paper, palm-leaf, deer-skin, cloth and sundry materials
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://culture.gov.in/khuda-baksh-oriental-public-library-patna' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'written on paper, palm-leaf, deer-skin, cloth and sundry materials'

facts.value: Khuda Bakhsh gave his whole personal collection to the people of Patna by a deed of trust.
facts.quote: donated his entire personal collection to the people of Patna by a deed of trust
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://culture.gov.in/khuda-baksh-oriental-public-library-patna' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'donated his entire personal collection to the people of Patna by a deed of trust'

facts.value: Gandhi visited in 1925 and wrote that the Quran and Shahnama manuscripts were an eternal feast for the eye.
facts.quote: The magnificent finish and the colouring about the decoration of Quran and Shahnama are an eternal feast for the eye
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/12/anger-over-plan-to-raze-part-of-iconic-indian-library-for-flyover' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'The magnificent finish and the colouring about the decoration of Quran and Shahnama are an eternal feast for the eye'

facts.value: The library building was Khuda Bakhsh's own residence, which he donated with his manuscript collection.
facts.quote: the library’s building used to be Khuda Bakhsh’s residence
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/12/anger-over-plan-to-raze-part-of-iconic-indian-library-for-flyover' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'building used to be Khuda Bakhsh'

events.label: The Curzon Reading Room was built in 1905, after Lord Curzon visited in 1903 and gave funds to expand the library.
events.quote: built in 1905 and named after the British viceroy to India, Lord Curzon, who visited the institution in 1903 and gave it funds to expand
